verdicts.flaw_description: Two of the four groups have measurement windows that end before treatment began: group one 'started 4 March' but is scored 'by 28 February', and group three 'started 5 September' but is scored 'by 30 August' (the season labels are also inverted, e.g. 'winter quarter, started 4 March'). An outcome recorded before the inhaler was ever given cannot be evidence of its effect.

The reported gains are computed on a self-selected subgroup: 'Averages cover the patients who kept up the home exercises, and a quarter of each intake let the home exercises lapse', so roughly 25% of each intake is dropped from the new-period average while the 'same ward a quarter earlier' baseline is not filtered the same way. Patients who keep up home exercises are exactly the ones expected to recover abduction fastest, so the 9-16 degree gains can come from the filter rather than the protocol.

The post-change defect rates are asymmetrically filtered: 'Rates cover the boards soldered on the new profile throughout, and about a tenth of each run's boards took one pass on the old profile', so ~10% of each run's boards are excluded from the new-profile figure while the 'same line a month earlier' comparison includes everything. Boards that needed an old-profile pass are the likely rework/problem boards, so removing them alone could produce the 4-7 percent apparent improvement.
